1.text: There was a man in tha land of Uz, whose name was Job; N dat man was perfect N upright, N one dat feared God, N eschewed evil.
N there were born 2 him seven sons N three daughters.

His substance also was seven thousand sheep, N three thousand camels, N five hundred yoke of oxen, N five hundred she asses, N a very great household; so dat dis man was tha greatest of all tha men of tha east.
N his sons went N feasted in their houses, every one his day; N sent N called 4 their three sisters 2 eat N 2 drink wit ’em.

N it was so, when tha days of their feasting were gone about, dat Job sent N sanctified ’em, N rose up early in tha morning, N offered burnt offerings according 2 tha number of ’em all: 4 Job said, It may be dat my sons have sinned, N cursed God in their hearts. like dis did Job continually.
Now there was a day when tha sons of God came 2 present themselves before tha LORD, N Satan came also among ’em.
N tha LORD said 2 Satan, from where come u? Then Satan answered tha LORD, N said, From goin 2 N fro in tha earth, N from walkin up N down in it.
N tha LORD said 2 Satan, have u considered my servant Job, dat there is none like him in tha earth, a perfect N an upright man, one dat fears God, N escheweth evil?
Then Satan answered tha LORD, N said, does Job fear God 4 nothing?
Have not u made an hedge about him, N about his house, N about all dat he has on every side? u have blessed tha work of his hands, N his substance is increased in tha land.
But put forth thine hand now, N touch all dat he has, N he will curse u 2 ur face.
N tha LORD said 2 Satan, look, all dat he has is in ur power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from tha presence of tha LORD.
N there was a day when his sons N his daughters were eatin N drinkin wine in their eldest brother’s house:
N there came a messenger 2 Job, N said, tha oxen were plowing, N tha asses feedin beside ’em:
N tha Sabeans fell upon ’em, N took ’em away; yeah, dey have killed tha servants wit tha edge of tha sword; N I only am escaped alone 2 tell u.
While he was yet speakin, there came also another, N said, tha fire of God is fallen from heaven, N has burned up tha sheep, N tha servants, N consumed ’em; N I only am escaped alone 2 tell u.

While he was yet speakin, there came also another, N said, tha Chaldeans made out three bands, N fell upon tha camels, N have carried ’em away, yeah, N killed tha servants wit tha edge of tha sword; N I only am escaped alone 2 tell u.
While he was yet speakin, there came also another, N said, ur sons N ur daughters were eatin N drinkin wine in their eldest brother’s house:
N, look, there came a great wind from tha wilderness, N struck tha four corners of tha house, N it fell upon tha young men, N dey r dead; N I only am escaped alone 2 tell u.
Then Job arose, N rent his mantle, N shaved his head, N fell down upon tha ground, N worshipped,
N said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, N naked shall I return there: tha LORD gave, N tha LORD has taken away; blessed be tha name of tha LORD.
In all dis Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.

2.text: Again there was a day when tha sons of God came 2 present themselves before tha LORD, N Satan came also among ’em 2 present himself before tha LORD.
N tha LORD said 2 Satan, From from where come u? N Satan answered tha LORD, N said, From goin 2 N fro in tha earth, N from walkin up N down in it.

N tha LORD said 2 Satan, have u considered my servant Job, dat there is none like him in tha earth, a perfect N an upright man, one dat fears God, N escheweth evil? N still he holds fast his integrity, although u movedst me against him, 2 destroy him without cause.
N Satan answered tha LORD, N said, Skin 4 skin, yeah, all dat a man has will he give 4 his life.
But put forth thine hand now, N touch his bone N his flesh, N he will curse u 2 ur face.
N tha LORD said 2 Satan, look, he is in thine hand; but save his life.
So went Satan forth from tha presence of tha LORD, N struck Job wit sore boils from tha sole of his foot 2 his crown.
N he took him a potsherd 2 scrape himself withal; N he sat down among tha ashes.
Then said his wife 2 him, do u still retain thine integrity? curse God, N die.
But he said 2 her, u speak as one of tha foolish women speaks. What? shall we receive good at tha hand of God, N shall we not receive evil? In all dis did not Job sin wit his lips.

Now when Job’s three friends heard of all dis evil dat was come upon him, dey came every one from his own place; Eliphaz tha Temanite, N Bildad tha Shuhite, N Zophar tha Naamathite: 4 dey had made an appointment together 2 come 2 mourn wit him N 2 comfort him.
N when dey lifted up their eyes afar off, N knew him not, dey lifted up their voice, N wept; N dey rent every one his mantle, N sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
So dey sat down wit him upon tha ground seven days N seven nights, N none spoke a word 2 him: 4 dey saw dat his grief was very great.

3.text: After dis opened Job his mouth, N cursed his day.
N Job spoke, N said,
Let tha day perish in which I was born, N tha night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.
Let dat day be darkness; don’t let God regard it from above, neither let tha light shine upon it.
Let darkness N tha shadow of death stain it; let a cloud live upon it; let tha blackness of tha day terrify it.
As 4 dat night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined 2 tha days of tha year, let it not come in2 tha number of tha months.
Look, let dat night be solitary, let no joyful voice come in it.
Let ’em curse it dat curse tha day, who r ready 2 raise up their mournin.
Let tha stars of tha twilight of it be dark; let it look 4 light, but have none; neither let it see tha dawning of tha day:
Because it shut not up tha doors of my mother’s womb, nor hid sorrow from my eyes.
Why died I not from tha womb? why did I not give up tha ghost when I came out of tha belly?
Why did tha knees prevent me? or why tha breasts dat I should suck?
4 now should I have lain still N been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,
Wit kings N counsellors of tha earth, which built desolate places 4 themselves;
Or wit princes dat had gold, who filled their houses wit silver:
Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.
There tha wicked cease from troublin; N there tha weary be at rest.
There tha prisoners rest together; dey hear not tha voice of tha oppressor.
Tha small N great r there; N tha servant is free from his master.
So is light given 2 him dat is in misery, N life 2 tha bitter in soul;
Which long 4 death, but it comes not; N dig 4 it more than 4 hid treasures;
Which rejoice exceedingly, N r glad, when dey can find tha grave?
Why is light given 2 a man whose way is hid, N whom God has hedged in?
4 my sighing comes before I eat, N my roarings r poured out like tha waterz.
4 tha thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, N dat which I was afraid of is come 2 me.
I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.

4.text: Then Eliphaz tha Temanite answered,
If we assay 2 commune wit u, will u be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speakin?
Look, u have instructed many, N u have strengthened tha weak hands.
Ur words have upholden him dat was fallin, N u have strengthened tha feeble knees.
But now it is come upon u, N u faintest; it touches u, N u r troubled.
Is not dis ur fear, ur confidence, ur hope, N tha uprightness of ur ways?
Remember, I pray u, who ever perished, bein innocent? or where were tha righteous cut off?
Even as I have seen, dey dat plow iniquity, N sow wickedness, reap tha same.
By tha blast of God dey perish, N by tha breath of his nostrils r dey consumed.
Tha roaring of tha lion, N tha voice of tha fierce lion, N tha teeth of tha young lions, r broken.
Tha old lion perishes 4 lack of prey, N tha stout lion’s whelps r scattered abroad.
Now a thing was secretly brought 2 me, N mine ear received a little of it.
In thoughts from tha visions of tha night, when deep sleep falls on men,
Fear came upon me, N tremblin, which made all my bones 2 shake.
Then a spirit passed before my face; tha hair of my flesh stood up:
It stood still, but I could not discern tha form of it: an image was before my eyes, there was silence, N I heard a voice, sayin,
Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?
Look, he put no trust in his servants; N his angels he charged wit folly:
How much less in ’em dat live in houses of clay, whose foundation is in tha dust, which r crushed before tha moth?
Dey r destroyed from morning 2 evening: dey perish 4 ever without any regarding it.
Does not their excellency which is in ’em go away? dey die, even without wisdom.

5.text: Call now, if there be any dat will answer u; N 2 which of tha saints will u turn?
4 wrath kills tha foolish man, N envy slayeth tha silly one.
I have seen tha foolish takin root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
His children r far from safety, N dey r crushed in tha gate, neither is there any 2 deliver ’em.
Whose harvest tha hungry eats up, N takes it even out of tha thorns, N tha robber swalloweth up their substance.
Although affliction comes not forth of tha dust, neither does trouble spring out of tha ground;
Yet man is born 2 trouble, as tha sparks fly upward.
I would seek 2 God, N 2 God would I commit my cause:
Which does great things N unsearchable; marvellous things without number:
Who gives rain upon tha earth, N sends waterz upon tha fields:
2 set up on high dose dat be low; dat dose which mourn may be exalted 2 safety.
He disappointeth tha devices of tha crafty, so dat their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
He takes tha wise in their own craftiness: N tha counsel of tha froward is carried headlong.
Dey meet wit darkness in tha daytime, N grope in tha noonday as in tha night.
But he saves tha poor from tha sword, from their mouth, N from tha hand of tha mighty.
So tha poor has hope, N iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
Look, happy is tha man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not u tha chastening of tha Almighty:
4 he makes sore, N binds up: he woundeth, N his hands make whole.
He shall deliver u in six troubles: yeah, in seven there shall no evil touch u.
In famine he shall redeem u from death: N in war from tha power of tha sword.
u will be hid from tha scourge of tha tongue: neither will u be afraid of destruction when it comes.
At destruction N famine u will laugh: neither will u be afraid of tha beasts of tha earth.
4 u will be in league wit tha stones of tha field: N tha beasts of tha field shall be at peace wit u.
N u will know dat ur tabernacle shall be in peace; N u will visit ur habitation, N will not sin.
u will know also dat ur seed shall be great, N thine offspring as tha grass of tha earth.
u will come 2 ur grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn comes in in his season.
Look dis, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, N know u it 4 ur good.

6.text: But Job answered,
Oh dat my grief were throughly weighed, N my calamity laid in tha balances together!
4 now it would be heavier than tha sand of tha sea: therefore my words r swallowed up.
4 tha arrows of tha Almighty r within me, tha poison whereof drinks up my spirit: tha terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
Does tha wild ass bray when he has grass? or loweth tha ox over his fodder?
Can dat which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in tha white of an egg?
Tha things dat my soul refused 2 touch r as my sorrowful food.
Oh dat I might have my request; N dat God would grant me tha thing dat I long 4!
Even dat it would please God 2 destroy me; dat he would let loose his hand, N cut me off!
Then should I yet have comfort; yeah, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; 4 I have not concealed tha words of tha Holy One.
What is my strength, dat I should hope? N what is mine end, dat I should prolong my life?
Is my strength tha strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?
Is not my help in me? N is wisdom driven quite from me?
2 him dat is afflicted pity should be showed from his friend; but he forsakes tha fear of tha Almighty.
My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, N as tha stream of brooks dey pass away;
Which r blackish by reason of tha ice, N in which tha snow is hid:
What time dey wax warm, dey vanish: when it is hot, dey r consumed out of their place.
Tha paths of their way r turned aside; dey go 2 nothing, N perish.
Tha troops of Tema looked, tha companies of Sheba waited 4 ’em.
Dey were confounded because dey had hoped; dey came there, N were ashamed.
4 now y’all r nothing; y’all see my castin down, N r afraid.
Did I say, Bring 2 me? or, Give a reward 4 me of ur substance?
Or, Deliver me from tha enemy’s hand? or, Redeem me from tha hand of tha mighty?
Teach me, N I will hold my tongue: N cause me 2 understand in which I have erred.
How forcible r right words! but what does ur arguing reprove?
Do y’all imagine 2 reprove words, N tha speeches of one dat is desperate, which r as wind?
Yeah, y’all overwhelm tha fatherless, N y’all dig a pit 4 ur friend.
Now therefore be content, look upon me; 4 it is evident 2 u if I lie.
Return, I pray u, let it not be iniquity; yeah, return again, my righteousness is in it.
Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?

7.text: Is there not an appointed time 2 man upon earth? r not his days also like tha days of an hireling?
As a servant earnestly desires tha shadow, N as an hireling looks 4 tha reward of his work:
So am I made 2 possess months of vanity, N wearisome nights r appointed 2 me.
When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, N tha night be gone? N I am full of tossings 2 N fro 2 tha dawning of tha day.
My flesh is clothed wit worms N clods of dust; my skin is broken, N become loathsome.
My days r swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, N r spent without hope.
O remember dat my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.
Tha eye of him dat has seen me shall see me no more: ur eyes r upon me, N I am not.
As tha cloud is consumed N vanisheth away: so he dat goes down 2 tha grave shall come up no more.
He shall return no more 2 his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in tha anguish of my spirit; I will complain in tha bitterness of my soul.
Am I a sea, or a whale, dat u set a watch over me?
When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
Then u scarest me wit dreams, N terrifiest me through visions:
So dat my soul chooseth strangling, N death rather than my life.
I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; 4 my days r vanity.
What is man, dat u should magnify him? N dat u should set thine heart upon him?
N dat u should visit him every morning, N try him every moment?
How long will u not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
I have sinned; what shall I do 2 u, O u preserver of men? why have u set me as a mark against u, so dat I am a burden 2 myself?
N why do u not pardon my transgression, N take away mine iniquity? 4 now shall I sleep in tha dust; N u will seek me in tha morning, but I shall not be.

8.text: Then answered Bildad tha Shuhite, N said,
How long will u speak dese things? N how long shall tha words of ur mouth be like a strong wind?
Does God pervert judgment? or does tha Almighty pervert justice?
If ur children have sinned against him, N he have cast ’em away 4 their transgression;
If u would seek 2 God betimes, N make ur supplication 2 tha Almighty;
If u were pure N upright; surely now he would awake 4 u, N make tha habitation of ur righteousness prosperous.
Though ur beginning was small, yet ur latter end should greatly increase.
4 enquire, I pray u, of tha former age, N prepare urself 2 tha search of their fathers:
(4 we r but of yesterday, N know nothing, because our days upon earth r a shadow:)
Shall not dey teach u, N tell u, N utter words out of their heart?
Can tha rush grow up without mire? can tha flag grow without water?
Whilst it is yet in his greenness, N not cut down, it withers before any other herb.
So r tha paths of all dat forget God; N tha hypocrite’s hope shall perish:
Whose hope shall be cut off, N whose trust shall be a spider’s web.
He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.
He is green before tha sun, N his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
His roots r wrapped about tha heap, N sees tha place of stones.
If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, sayin, I have not seen u.
Look, dis is tha joy of his way, N out of tha earth shall others grow.
Look, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help tha evil doers:
Till he fill ur mouth wit laughin, N ur lips wit rejoicin.
Dey dat hate u shall be clothed wit shame; N tha livin place of tha wicked shall come 2 nothing.

9.text: Then Job answered,
I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just wit God?
If he will contend wit him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.
He is wise in heart, N mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, N has prospered?
Which removeth tha mountains, N dey know not: which overturneth ’em in his anger.
Which shakes tha earth out of her place, N tha pillars of it tremble.
Which commands tha sun, N it rises not; N sealeth up tha stars.
Which alone spreads out tha heavenz, N treads upon tha waves of tha sea.
Which makes Arcturus, Orion, N Pleiades, N tha chambers of tha south.
Which does great things past finding out; yeah, N wonders without number.
Look, he goes by me, N I see him not: he passes on also, but I perceive him not.
Look, he takes away, who can hinder him? who will say 2 him, What do u?
If God will not withdraw his anger, tha proud helpers do stoop under him.
How much less shall I answer him, N choose out my words 2 reason wit him?
Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication 2 my judge.
If I had called, N he had answered me; yet would I not believe dat he had listened 2 my voice.
4 he breaks me wit a tempest, N multiplieth my wounds without cause.
He will not suffer me 2 take my breath, but fills me wit bitterness.
If I speak of strength, look, he is strong: N if of judgment, who shall set me a time 2 plead?
If I justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
Dis is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroys tha perfect N tha wicked.
If tha scourge kill suddenly, he will laugh at tha trial of tha innocent.
Tha earth is given in2 tha hand of tha wicked: he covers tha faces of tha judges of it; if not, where, N who is he?
Now my days r swifter than a post: dey flee away, dey see no good.
Dey r passed away as tha swift ships: as tha eagle dat hurries 2 tha prey.
If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, N comfort myself:
I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know dat u will not hold me innocent.
If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?
If I wash myself wit snow water, N make my hands never so clean;
Yet will u plunge me in tha ditch, N my own clothes shall abhor me.
4 he is not a man, as I am, dat I should answer him, N we should come together in judgment.
Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, dat might lay his hand upon us both.
Let him take his rod away from me, N don’t let his fear terrify me:
Then would I speak, N not fear him; but it is not so wit me.

10.text: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in tha bitterness of my soul.
I will say 2 God, Do not condemn me; show me so u contendest wit me.
Is it good 2 u dat u should oppress, dat u should despise tha work of thine hands, N shine upon tha counsel of tha wicked?
Have u eyes of flesh? or see u as man sees?
R ur days as tha days of man? r ur years as man’s days,
Dat u enquirest after mine iniquity, N search after my sin?
u know dat I am not wicked; N there is none dat can deliver out of thine hand.
Thine hands have made me N fashioned me together round about; yet u do destroy me.
Remember, I beg u, dat u have made me as tha clay; N will u bring me in2 dust again?
Have u not poured me out as milk, N curdled me like cheese?
u have clothed me wit skin N flesh, N have fenced me wit bones N sinews.
u have granted me life N favour, N ur visitation has preserved my spirit.
N dese things have u hid in thine heart: I know dat dis is wit u.
If I sin, then u markest me, N u will not acquit me from mine iniquity.
If I be wicked, woe 2 me; N if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see u mine affliction;
4 it increases. u huntest me as a fierce lion: N again u show urself marvellous upon me.
u renewest ur witnesses against me, N increase thine indignation upon me; changes N war r against me.
So then have u brought me forth out of tha womb? Oh dat I had given up tha ghost, N no eye had seen me!
I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from tha womb 2 tha grave.
R not my days few? cease then, N let me alone, dat I may take comfort a little,
Before I go from where I shall not return, even 2 tha land of darkness N tha shadow of death;
A land of darkness, as darkness itself; N of tha shadow of death, without any order, N where tha light is as darkness.

11.text: Then answered Zophar tha Naamathite, N said,
Should not tha crowd of words be answered? N should a man full of talk be justified?
Should ur lies make men hold their peace? N when u mockest, shall no man make u ashamed?
4 u have said, My doctrine is pure, N I am clean in ur eyes.
But oh dat God would speak, N open his lips against u;
N dat he would show u tha secrets of wisdom, dat dey r double 2 dat which is! Know therefore dat God exacteth of u less than thine iniquity deserveth.
Can u by searchin find out God? can u find out tha Almighty 2 perfection?
It is as high as heaven; what can u do? deeper than hell; what can u know?
Tha measure of it is longer than tha earth, N broader than tha sea.
If he cut off, N shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?
4 he knows vain men: he sees wickedness also; will he not then consider it?
4 vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.
If u prepare thine heart, N stretch out thine hands toward him;
If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, N don’t let wickedness live in ur tabernacles.
4 then will u lift up ur face without spot; yeah, u will be stedfast, N will not fear:
Because u will forget ur misery, N remember it as waterz dat pass away:
N thine age shall be clearer than tha noonday; u will shine forth, u will be as tha morning.
N u will be secure, because there is hope; yeah, u will dig about u, N u will take ur rest in safety.
Also u will lie down, N none shall make u afraid; yeah, many shall make suit 2 u.
But tha eyes of tha wicked shall fail, N dey shall not escape, N their hope shall be as tha givin up of tha ghost.

12.text: N Job answered,
No doubt but y’all r tha people, N wisdom shall die wit u.
But I have understanding as well as u; I am not inferior 2 u: yeah, who knows not such things as dese?
I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calls upon God, N he answers him: tha just upright man is laughed 2 scorn.
He dat is ready 2 slip wit his feet is as a lamp despised in tha thought of him dat is at ease.
Tha tabernacles of robbers prosper, N dey dat provoke God r secure; in2 whose hand God brings abundantly.
But ask now tha beasts, N dey shall teach u; N tha fowls of tha air, N dey shall tell u:
Or speak 2 tha earth, N it shall teach u: N tha fishes of tha sea shall declare 2 u.
Who knows not in all dese dat tha hand of tha LORD has wrought dis?
In whose hand is tha soul of every livin thing, N tha breath of all mankind.
Does not tha ear try words? N tha mouth taste his food?
Wit tha ancient is wisdom; N in length of days understanding.
Wit him is wisdom N strength, he has counsel N understanding.
Look, he breaks down, N it cannot be built again: he shuts up a man, N there can be no opening.
Look, he withholdeth tha waterz, N dey dry up: also he sends ’em out, N dey overturn tha earth.
Wit him is strength N wisdom: tha deceived N tha deceiver r his.
He leads counsellors away spoiled, N makes tha judges fools.
He looseth tha bond of kings, N girdeth their loins wit a girdle.
He leads princes away spoiled, N overthroweth tha mighty.
He removeth away tha speech of tha trusty, N takes away tha understanding of tha aged.
He pours contempt upon princes, N weakeneth tha strength of tha mighty.
He discovereth deep things out of darkness, N brings out 2 light tha shadow of death.
He increases tha nations, N destroys ’em: he enlargeth tha nations, N straiteneth ’em again.
He takes away tha heart of tha chief of tha people of tha earth, N causes ’em 2 wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
Dey grope in tha dark without light, N he makes ’em 2 stagger like a drunken man.

13.text: Look, mine eye has seen all dis, mine ear has heard N understood it.
What y’all know, tha same do I know also: I am not inferior 2 u.
Surely I would speak 2 tha Almighty, N I desire 2 reason wit God.
But y’all r forgers of lies, y’all r all physicians of no value.
O dat y’all would altogether hold ur peace! N it should be ur wisdom.
Hear now my reasoning, N listen 2 tha pleadings of my lips.
Will y’all speak wickedly 4 God? N talk deceitfully 4 him?
Will y’all accept his person? will y’all contend 4 God?
Is it good dat he should search u out? or as one man mocketh another, do y’all so mock him?
He will surely reprove u, if y’all do secretly accept persons.
Shall not his excellency make u afraid? N his dread fall upon u?
Ur remembrances r like 2 ashes, ur bodies 2 bodies of clay.
Hold ur peace, let me alone, dat I may speak, N let come on me what will.
So do I take my flesh in my teeth, N put my life in mine hand?
Though he kill me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain my own ways before him.
He also shall be my salvation: 4 an hypocrite shall not come before him.
Hear diligently my speech, N my declaration wit ur ears.
Look now, I have ordered my cause; I know dat I shall be justified.
Who is he dat will plead wit me? 4 now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up tha ghost.
Only do not two things 2 me: then will I not hide myself from u.
Withdraw thine hand far from me: N don’t let ur dread make me afraid.
Then call u, N I will answer: or let me speak, N answer u me.
How many r mine iniquities N sins? make me 2 know my transgression N my sin.
So hide u ur face, N hold me 4 thine opp?
Will u break a leaf driven 2 N fro? N will u pursue tha dry stubble?
4 u writest bitter things against me, N make me 2 possess tha iniquities of my youth.
u put my feet also in tha stocks, N look narrowly 2 all my paths; u set a print upon tha heels of my feet.
N he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment dat is moth eaten.

14.text: Man dat is born of a woman is of few days, N full of trouble.
He comes forth like a flower, N is cut down: he flees also as a shadow, N continueth not.
N do u open ur eyes upon such an one, N bring me in2 judgment wit u?
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
Seein his days r determined, tha number of his months r wit u, u have appointed his bounds dat he cannot pass;
Turn from him, dat he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.
4 there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, dat it will sprout again, N dat tha tender branch of it will not cease.
Though tha root of it wax old in tha earth, N tha stock of it die in tha ground;
Yet through tha scent of water it will bud, N bring forth boughs like a plant.
But man dies, N wasteth away: yeah, man gives up tha ghost, N where is he?
As tha waterz fail from tha sea, N tha flood decayeth N drieth up:
So man lies down, N rises not: till tha heavenz be no more, dey shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.
O dat u would hide me in tha grave, dat u would keep me secret, until ur wrath be past, dat u would appoint me a set time, N remember me!
If a man die, shall he live again? all tha days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
u will call, N I will answer u: u will have a desire 2 tha work of thine hands.
4 now u numberest my steps: do u not watch over my sin?
My transgression is sealed up in a bag, N u sewest up mine iniquity.
N surely tha mountain fallin comes 2 nothing, N tha rock is removed out of his place.
Tha waterz wear tha stones: u washest away tha things which grow out of tha dust of tha earth; N u destroy tha hope of man.
u prevailest 4 ever against him, N he passes: u changest his countenance, N send him away.
His sons come 2 honour, N he knows it not; N dey r brought low, but he perceiveth it not of ’em.
But his flesh upon him shall have pain, N his soul within him shall mourn.

15.text: Then answered Eliphaz tha Temanite, N said,
Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, N fill his belly wit tha east wind?
Should he reason wit unprofitable talk? or wit speeches wherewith he can do no good?
Yeah, u cast off fear, N restrainest prayer before God.
4 ur mouth utters thine iniquity, N u choosest tha tongue of tha crafty.
Ur own mouth condemneth u, N not I: yeah, ur own lips testify against u.
R u tha first man dat was born? or were u made before tha hills?
Have u heard tha secret of God? N do u restrain wisdom 2 urself?
What know u, dat we know not? what understand u, which is not in us?
Wit us r both tha grayheaded N very aged men, much elder than ur father.
R tha consolations of God small wit u? is there any secret thing wit u?
Why does thine heart carry u away? N what do ur eyes wink at,
Dat u turn ur spirit against God, N lettest such words go out of ur mouth?
What is man, dat he should be clean? N he which is born of a woman, dat he should be righteous?
Look, he puts no trust in his saints; yeah, tha heavenz r not clean in his sight.
How much more abominable N filthy is man, which drinks iniquity like water?
I will show u, hear me; N dat which I have seen I will declare;
Which wise men have told from their fathers, N have not hid it:
2 whom alone tha earth was given, N no stranger passed among ’em.
Tha wicked man labors wit pain all his days, N tha number of years is hidden 2 tha oppressor.
A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity tha destroyer shall come upon him.
He believes not dat he shall return out of darkness, N he is waited 4 of tha sword.
He wanders abroad 4 bread, sayin, Where is it? he knows dat tha day of darkness is ready at his hand.
Trouble N anguish shall make him afraid; dey shall prevail against him, as a king ready 2 tha battle.
4 he stretches out his hand against God, N strengthens himself against tha Almighty.
He runs upon him, even on his neck, upon tha thick bosses of his bucklers:
Because he covers his face wit his fatness, N makes collops of fat on his flanks.
N he lives in desolate citiez, N in houses which no man inhabiteth, which r ready 2 become heaps.
He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong tha perfection of it upon tha earth.
He shall not depart out of darkness; tha flame shall dry up his branches, N by tha breath of his mouth shall he go away.
Don’t let him dat is deceived trust in vanity: 4 vanity shall be his recompence.
It shall be accomplished before his time, N his branch shall not be green.
He shall shake off his unripe grape as tha vine, N shall cast off his flower as tha olive.
4 tha congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, N fire shall consume tha tabernacles of bribery.
Dey conceive mischief, N bring forth vanity, N their belly prepareth deceit.

16.text: Then Job answered,
I have heard many such things: miserable comforters r y’all all.
Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth u dat u answer?
I also could speak as y’all do: if ur soul were in my soul’s stead, I could heap up words against u, N shake mine head at u.
But I would strengthen u wit my mouth, N tha movin of my lips should asswage ur grief.
Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: N though I forbear, what am I eased?
But now he has made me weary: u have made desolate all my company.
N u have filled me wit wrinkles, which is a witness against me: N my leanness risin up in me bears witness 2 my face.
He tears me in his wrath, who hates me: he gnasheth upon me wit his teeth; mine opp sharpeneth his eyes upon me.
Dey have gaped upon me wit their mouth; dey have struck me upon tha cheek reproachfully; dey have gathered themselves together against me.
God has delivered me 2 tha ungodly, N turned me over in2 tha hands of tha wicked.
I was at ease, but he has broken me asunder: he has also taken me by my neck, N shaken me 2 pieces, N set me up 4 his mark.
His archers compass me round about, he clings my reins asunder, N does not spare; he pours out my gall upon tha ground.
He breaks me wit breach upon breach, he runs upon me like a giant.
I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, N defiled my horn in tha dust.
My face is foul wit weepin, N on my eyelids is tha shadow of death;
Not 4 any injustice in mine hands: also my prayer is pure.
O earth, cover not u my blood, N let my cry have no place.
Also now, look, my witness is in heaven, N my record is on high.
My friends scorn me: but mine eye pours out tears 2 God.
O dat one might plead 4 a man wit God, as a man pleadeth 4 his neighbour!
When a few years r come, then I shall go tha way from where I shall not return.

17.text: My breath is corrupt, my days r extinct, tha graves r ready 4 me.
R there not mockers wit me? N does not mine eye continue in their provocation?
Lay down now, put me in a surety wit u; who is he dat will strike hands wit me?
4 u have hid their heart from understanding: therefore will u not exalt ’em.
He dat speaks flattery 2 his friends, even tha eyes of his children shall fail.
He has made me also a byword of tha people; N aforetime I was as a tabret.
Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, N all my members r as a shadow.
Upright men shall be astonied at dis, N tha innocent shall stir up himself against tha hypocrite.
Tha righteous also shall hold on his way, N he dat has clean hands shall be stronger N stronger.
But as 4 u all, do y’all return, N come now: 4 I cannot find one wise man among u.
My days r past, my purposes r broken off, even tha thoughts of my heart.
Dey change tha night in2 day: tha light is short because of darkness.
If I wait, tha grave is mine house: I have made my bed in tha darkness.
I have said 2 corruption, u r my father: 2 tha worm, u r my mother, N my sister.
N where is now my hope? as 4 my hope, who shall see it?
Dey shall go down 2 tha bars of tha pit, when our rest together is in tha dust.

18.text: Then answered Bildad tha Shuhite, N said,
How long will it be ere y’all make an end of words? mark, N afterwards we will speak.
So r we counted as beasts, N reputed vile in ur sight?
He tears himself in his anger: shall tha earth be forsaken 4 u? N shall tha rock be removed out of his place?
Yeah, tha light of tha wicked shall be put out, N tha spark of his fire shall not shine.
Tha light shall be dark in his tabernacle, N his candle shall be put out wit him.
Tha steps of his strength shall be straitened, N his own counsel shall cast him down.
4 he is cast in2 a net by his own feet, N he walks upon a snare.
Tha gin shall take him by tha heel, N tha robber shall prevail against him.
Tha snare is laid 4 him in tha ground, N a trap 4 him in tha way.
Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, N shall drive him 2 his feet.
His strength shall be hungerbitten, N destruction shall be ready at his side.
It shall devour tha strength of his skin: even tha firstborn of death shall devour his strength.
His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, N it shall bring him 2 tha king of terrors.
It shall live in his tabernacle, because it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
His roots shall be dried up beneath, N above shall his branch be cut off.
His remembrance shall perish from tha earth, N he shall have no name in tha street.
He shall be driven from light in2 darkness, N chased out of tha world.
He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.
Dey dat come after him shall be astonied at his day, as dey dat went before were affrighted.
Surely such r tha dwellings of tha wicked, N dis is tha place of him dat knows not God.

19.text: Then Job answered,
How long will y’all vex my soul, N break me in pieces wit words?
Dese ten times have y’all reproached me: y’all r not ashamed dat y’all make y’all strange 2 me.
N be it indeed dat I have erred, mine error remains wit myself.
If indeed y’all will magnify y’all against me, N plead against me my reproach:
Know now dat God has overthrown me, N has compassed me wit his net.
Look, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but there is no judgment.
He has fenced up my way dat I cannot pass, N he has set darkness in my paths.
He has stripped me of my glory, N taken tha crown from my head.
He has destroyed me on every side, N I am gone: N mine hope has he removed like a tree.
He has also kindled his wrath against me, N he counteth me 2 him as one of his opps.
His troops come together, N raise up their way against me, N encamp round about my tabernacle.
He has put my brothers far from me, N mine acquaintance r for real estranged from me.
My kinsfolk have failed, N my familiar friends have forgotten me.
Dey dat live in mine house, N my maids, count me 4 a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.
I called my servant, N he gave me no answer; I intreated him wit my mouth.
My breath is strange 2 my wife, though I intreated 4 tha children’s sake of my own body.
Yeah, young children despised me; I arose, N dey spoke against me.
All my inward friends abhorred me: N dey whom I loved r turned against me.
My bone clings 2 my skin N 2 my flesh, N I am escaped wit tha skin of my teeth.
Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O y’all my friends; 4 tha hand of God has touched me.
Why do y’all persecute me as God, N r not satisfied wit my flesh?
Oh dat my words were now written! oh dat dey were printed in a book!
Dat dey were graven wit an iron pen N lead in tha rock 4 ever!
4 I know dat my redeemer lives, N dat he shall stand at tha latter day upon tha earth:
N though after my skin worms destroy dis body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
Whom I shall see 4 myself, N my eyes shall look, N not another; though my reins be consumed within me.
But y’all should say, Why persecute we him, seein tha root of tha matter is found in me?
Be y’all afraid of tha sword: 4 wrath brings tha punishments of tha sword, dat y’all may know there is a judgment.

20.text: Then answered Zophar tha Naamathite, N said,
Therefore do my thoughts cause me 2 answer, N 4 dis I make haste.
I have heard tha check of my reproach, N tha spirit of my understanding causes me 2 answer.
Know u not dis of old, since man was placed upon earth,
Dat tha triumphing of tha wicked is short, N tha joy of tha hypocrite but 4 a moment?
Though his excellency mount up 2 tha heavenz, N his head reach 2 tha clouds;
Yet he shall perish 4 ever like his own dung: dey which have seen him shall say, Where is he?
He shall fly away as a dream, N shall not be found: yeah, he shall be chased away as a vision of tha night.
Tha eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more look him.
His children shall seek 2 please tha poor, N his hands shall restore their goods.
His bones r full of tha sin of his youth, which shall lie down wit him in tha dust.
Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue;
Though he spare it, N forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:
Yet his food in his bowels is turned, it is tha gall of asps within him.
He has swallowed down riches, N he shall vomit ’em up again: God shall cast ’em out of his belly.
He shall suck tha poison of asps: tha viper’s tongue shall kill him.
He shall not see tha rivers, tha floods, tha brooks of honey N butter.
Dat which he laboured 4 shall he restore, N shall not swallow it down: according 2 his substance shall tha restitution be, N he shall not rejoice in it.
Because he has oppressed N has forsaken tha poor; because he has violently taken away an house which he builded not;
Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of dat which he desired.
There shall none of his food be left; therefore shall no man look 4 his goods.
In tha fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of tha wicked shall come upon him.
When he is about 2 fill his belly, God shall cast tha fury of his wrath upon him, N shall rain it upon him while he is eatin.
He shall flee from tha iron weapon, N tha bow of steel shall strike him through.
It is drawn, N comes out of tha body; yeah, tha glittering sword comes out of his gall: terrors r upon him.
All darkness shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill wit him dat is left in his tabernacle.
Tha heaven shall reveal his iniquity; N tha earth shall rise up against him.
Tha increase of his house shall depart, N his goods shall flow away in tha day of his wrath.
Dis is tha portion of a wicked man from God, N tha heritage appointed 2 him by God.

21.text: But Job answered,
Hear diligently my speech, N let dis be ur consolations.
Suffer me dat I may speak; N after dat I have spoken, mock on.
As 4 me, is my complaint 2 man? N if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled?
Mark me, N be astonished, N lay ur hand upon ur mouth.
Even when I remember I am afraid, N tremblin takes hold on my flesh.
So do tha wicked live, become old, yeah, r mighty in power?
Their seed is established in their sight wit ’em, N their offspring before their eyes.
Their houses r safe from fear, neither is tha rod of God upon ’em.
Their bull gendereth, N fails not; their cow calveth, N casts not her calf.
Dey send forth their little ones like a flock, N their children dance.
Dey take tha timbrel N harp, N rejoice at tha sound of tha organ.
Dey spend their days in wealth, N in a moment go down 2 tha grave.
Therefore dey say 2 God, Depart from us; 4 we desire not tha knowledge of ur ways.
What is tha Almighty, dat we should serve him? N what profit should we have, if we pray 2 him?
Look, their good is not in their hand: tha counsel of tha wicked is far from me.
How oft is tha candle of tha wicked put out! N how oft comes their destruction upon ’em! God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
Dey r as stubble before tha wind, N as chaff dat tha storm carrieth away.
God lays up his iniquity 4 his children: he rewards him, N he shall know it.
His eyes shall see his destruction, N he shall drink of tha wrath of tha Almighty.
4 what pleasure has he in his house after him, when tha number of his months is cut off in tha midst?
Shall any teach God knowledge? seein he judges dose dat r high.
One dies in his full strength, bein wholly at ease N quiet.
His breasts r full of milk, N his bones r moistened wit marrow.
N another dies in tha bitterness of his soul, N never eats wit pleasure.
Dey shall lie down alike in tha dust, N tha worms shall cover ’em.
Look, I know ur thoughts, N tha devices which y’all wrongfully imagine against me.
4 y’all say, Where is tha house of tha prince? N where r tha livin places of tha wicked?
Have y’all not asked ’em dat go by tha way? N do y’all not know their tokens,
Dat tha wicked is reserved 2 tha day of destruction? dey shall be brought forth 2 tha day of wrath.
Who shall declare his way 2 his face? N who shall repay him what he has done?
Yet shall he be brought 2 tha grave, N shall remain in tha tomb.
Tha clods of tha valley shall be sweet 2 him, N every man shall draw after him, as there r innumerable before him.
How then comfort y’all me in vain, seein in ur answers there remains falsehood?

22.text: Then Eliphaz tha Temanite answered,
Can a man be profitable 2 God, as he dat is wise may be profitable 2 himself?
Is it any pleasure 2 tha Almighty, dat u r righteous? or is it gain 2 him, dat u make ur ways perfect?
Will he reprove u 4 fear of u? will he enter wit u in2 judgment?
Is not ur wickedness great? N thine iniquities infinite?
4 u have taken a pledge from ur brother 4 nothing, N stripped tha naked of their clothing.
u have not given water 2 tha weary 2 drink, N u have withholden bread from tha hungry.
But as 4 tha mighty man, he had tha earth; N tha honourable man lived in it.
u have sent widows away empty, N tha arms of tha fatherless have been broken.
Therefore snares r round about u, N sudden fear troubles u;
Or darkness, dat u can not see; N abundance of waterz cover u.
Is not God in tha height of heaven? N look tha height of tha stars, how high dey r!
N u sayest, How does God know? can he judge through tha dark cloud?
Thick clouds r a covering 2 him, dat he sees not; N he walks in tha circuit of heaven.
Have u marked tha old way which wicked men have trodden?
Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown wit a flood:
Which said 2 God, Depart from us: N what can tha Almighty do 4 ’em?
Yet he filled their houses wit good things: but tha counsel of tha wicked is far from me.
Tha righteous see it, N r glad: N tha innocent laugh ’em 2 scorn.
Whereas our substance is not cut down, but tha remnant of ’em tha fire consumeth.
Acquaint now urself wit him, N be at peace: by dat good shall come 2 u.
Receive, I pray u, tha law from his mouth, N lay up his words in thine heart.
If u return 2 tha Almighty, u will be built up, u will put away iniquity far from ur tabernacles.
Then will u lay up gold as dust, N tha gold of Ophir as tha stones of tha brooks.
Yeah, tha Almighty shall be ur defence, N u will have plenty of silver.
4 then will u have ur delight in tha Almighty, N will lift up ur face 2 God.
u will make ur prayer 2 him, N he shall hear u, N u will pay ur vows.
u will also decree a thing, N it will be established 2 u: N tha light shall shine upon ur ways.
When men r cast down, then u will say, There is liftin up; N he shall save tha humble person.
He shall deliver tha island of tha innocent: N it is delivered by tha pureness of thine hands.

23.text: Even 2 day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
Oh dat I knew where I might find him! dat I might come even 2 his seat!
I would order my cause before him, N fill my mouth wit arguments.
I would know tha words which he would answer me, N understand what he would say 2 me.
Will he plead against me wit his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.
There tha righteous might dispute wit him; so should I be delivered 4 ever from my judge.
Look, I go forward, but he is not there; N backward, but I cannot perceive him:
On tha left hand, where he does work, but I cannot look him: he hides himself on tha right hand, dat I cannot see him:
But he knows tha way dat I take: when he has tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
My foot has held his steps, his way have I kept, N not declined.
Neither have I gone back from tha commandment of his lips; I have esteemed tha words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
But he is in one mind, N who can turn him? N what his soul desires, even dat he does.
4 he performeth tha thing dat is appointed 4 me: N many such things r wit him.
Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him.
4 God makes my heart soft, N tha Almighty troubles me:
Because I was not cut off before tha darkness, neither has he covered tha darkness from my face.

24.text: Why, seein times r not hidden from tha Almighty, do dey dat know him not see his days?
Some remove tha landmarks; dey violently take away flocks, N feed of it.
Dey drive away tha ass of tha fatherless, dey take tha widow’s ox 4 a pledge.
Dey turn tha needy out of tha way: tha poor of tha earth hide themselves together.
Look, as wild asses in tha desert, go dey forth 2 their work; risin betimes 4 a prey: tha wilderness yieldeth food 4 ’em N 4 their children.
Dey reap every one his corn in tha field: N dey gather tha vintage of tha wicked.
Dey cause tha naked 2 lodge without clothing, dat dey have no covering in tha cold.
Dey r wet wit tha showers of tha mountains, N embrace tha rock 4 want of a shelter.
Dey pluck tha fatherless from tha breast, N take a pledge of tha poor.
Dey cause him 2 go naked without clothing, N dey take away tha sheaf from tha hungry;
Which make oil within their walls, N tread their winepresses, N suffer thirst.
Men groan from out of tha city, N tha soul of tha wounded cries out: yet God lays not folly 2 ’em.
Dey r of dose dat rebel against tha light; dey know not tha ways of it, nor abide in tha paths of it.
Tha murderer risin wit tha light kills tha poor N needy, N in tha night is as a thief.
Tha eye also of tha adulterer waits 4 tha twilight, sayin, No eye shall see me: N disguiseth his face.
In tha dark dey dig through houses, which dey had marked 4 themselves in tha daytime: dey know not tha light.
4 tha morning is 2 ’em even as tha shadow of death: if one know ’em, dey r in tha terrors of tha shadow of death.
He is swift as tha waterz; their portion is cursed in tha earth: he beholdeth not tha way of tha vineyards.
Drought N heat consume tha snow waterz: so does tha grave dose which have sinned.
Tha womb shall forget him; tha worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; N wickedness shall be broken as a tree.
He evil entreateth tha barren dat bears not: N does not good 2 tha widow.
He draws also tha mighty wit his power: he rises up, N no man is sure of life.
Though it be given him 2 be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes r upon their ways.
Dey r exalted 4 a little while, but r gone N brought low; dey r taken out of tha way as all other, N cut off as tha tops of tha ears of corn.
N if it don’t be so now, who will make me a liar, N make my speech nothing worth?

25.text: Then answered Bildad tha Shuhite, N said,
Dominion N fear r wit him, he makes peace in his high places.
Is there any number of his armies? N upon whom does not his light arise?
How then can man be justified wit God? or how can he be clean dat is born of a woman?
Look even 2 tha moon, N it shines not; yeah, tha stars r not pure in his sight.
How much less man, dat is a worm? N tha son of man, which is a worm?

26.text: How have u helped him dat is without power? how save u tha arm dat has no strength?
How have u counselled him dat has no wisdom? N how have u plentifully declared tha thing as it is?
2 whom have u uttered words? N whose spirit came from u?
Dead things r formed from under tha waterz, N tha inhabitants of it.
Hell is naked before him, N destruction has no covering.
He stretches out tha north over tha empty place, N hangeth tha earth upon nothing.
He binds up tha waterz in his thick clouds; N tha cloud is not rent under ’em.
He holds back tha face of his throne, N spreads his cloud upon it.
He has compassed tha waterz wit bounds, until tha day N night come 2 an end.
Tha pillars of heaven tremble N r astonished at his reproof.
He divides tha sea wit his power, N by his understanding he strikes through tha proud.
By his spirit he has garnished tha heavenz; his hand has formed tha crooked serpent.
Look, dese r parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but tha thunder of his power who can understand?

27.text: Moreover Job continued his parable, N said,
As God lives, who has taken away my judgment; N tha Almighty, who has vexed my soul;
All tha while my breath is in me, N tha spirit of God is in my nostrils;
My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.
God forbid dat I should justify u: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
My righteousness I hold fast, N will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.
Let mine opp be as tha wicked, N he dat rises up against me as tha unrighteous.
4 what is tha hope of tha hypocrite, though he has gained, when God takes away his soul?
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes upon him?
Will he delight himself in tha Almighty? will he always call upon God?
I will teach u by tha hand of God: dat which is wit tha Almighty will I not conceal.
Look, all y’all y’all have seen it; why then r y’all like dis altogether vain?
Dis is tha portion of a wicked man wit God, N tha heritage of oppressors, which dey shall receive of tha Almighty.
If his children be multiplied, it is 4 tha sword: N his offspring shall not be satisfied wit bread.
Dose dat remain of him shall be buried in death: N his widows shall not weep.
Though he heap up silver as tha dust, N prepare clothing as tha clay;
He may prepare it, but tha just shall put it on, N tha innocent shall divide tha silver.
He builds his house as a moth, N as a booth dat tha keeper makes.
Tha rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he opens his eyes, N he is not.
Terrors take hold on him as waterz, a tempest stealeth him away in tha night.
Tha east wind carrieth him away, N he departs: N as a storm hurleth him out of his place.
4 God shall cast upon him, N not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
Men shall clap their hands at him, N shall hiss him out of his place.

28.text: Surely there is a vein 4 tha silver, N a place 4 gold where dey fine it.
Iron is taken out of tha earth, N brass is molten out of tha stone.
He sets an end 2 darkness, N searches out all perfection: tha stones of darkness, N tha shadow of death.
Tha flood breaks out from tha inhabitant; even tha waterz forgotten of tha foot: dey r dried up, dey r gone away from men.
As 4 tha earth, out of it comes bread: N under it is turned up as it were fire.
Tha stones of it r tha place of sapphires: N it has dust of gold.
There is a path which no fowl knows, N which tha vulture’s eye has not seen:
Tha lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor tha fierce lion passed by it.
He puts forth his hand upon tha rock; he overturneth tha mountains by tha roots.
He cuts out rivers among tha rocks; N his eye sees every precious thing.
He binds tha floods from overflowing; N tha thing dat is hid brings he forth 2 light.
But where shall wisdom be found? N where is tha place of understanding?
Man knows not tha price of it; neither is it found in tha land of tha livin.
Tha depth says, It is not in me: N tha sea says, It is not wit me.
It cannot be got 4 gold, neither shall silver be weighed 4 tha price of it.
It cannot be valued wit tha gold of Ophir, wit tha precious onyx, or tha sapphire.
Tha gold N tha crystal cannot equal it: N tha exchange of it shall not be 4 jewels of fine gold.
No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: 4 tha price of wisdom is above rubies.
Tha topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued wit pure gold.
From where then comes wisdom? N where is tha place of understanding?
Seein it is hid from tha eyes of all livin, N kept close from tha fowls of tha air.
Destruction N death say, We have heard tha fame of it wit our ears.

29.text: Moreover Job continued his parable, N said,

30.text: But now dey dat r younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained 2 have set wit tha dogs of my flock.
Yeah, whereto might tha strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?
4 want N famine dey were solitary; fleein in2 tha wilderness in former time desolate N waste.
Who cut up mallows by tha bushes, N juniper roots 4 their food.

By tha great force of my disease is my garment changed: it binds me about as tha collar of my coat.
He has cast me in2 tha mire, N I am become like dust N ashes.
I cry 2 u, N u do not hear me: I stand up, N u regard me not.

u lift me up 2 tha wind; u cause me 2 ride upon it, N dissolvest my substance.

31.text: I made a covenant wit my eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
4 what portion of God is there from above? N what inheritance of tha Almighty from on high?
Is not destruction 2 tha wicked? N a strange punishment 2 tha workers of iniquity?

4 dis is an heinous crime; yeah, it is an iniquity 2 be punished by tha judges.
4 it is a fire dat consumeth 2 destruction, N would root out all mine increase.
If I did despise tha cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when dey contended wit me;

If I have withheld tha poor from their desire, or have caused tha eyes of tha widow 2 fail;
Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, N tha fatherless has not eaten of it;
(4 from my youth he was brought up wit me, as wit a father, N I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)
If I have seen any perish 4 want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

4 destruction from God was a terror 2 me, N by reason of his highness I could not endure.

If I beheld tha sun when it shined, or tha moon walkin in brightness;
N my heart has been secretly enticed, or my mouth has kissed my hand:
Dis also were an iniquity 2 be punished by tha judge: 4 I should have denied tha God dat is above.
If I rejoiced at tha destruction of him dat hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:
Neither have I suffered my mouth 2 sin by wishing a curse 2 his soul.
If tha men of my tabernacle said not, Oh dat we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.
Tha stranger did not lodge in tha street: but I opened my doors 2 tha traveller.
If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hidin mine iniquity in my bosom:

32.text: So dese three men ceased 2 answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then was kindled tha wrath of Elihu tha son of Barachel tha Buzite, of tha kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.

N Elihu tha son of Barachel tha Buzite answered, I am young, N y’all r very old; so I was afraid, N dared not show u mine opinion.

Therefore I said, listen 2 me; I also will show mine opinion.

Yeah, I attended 2 u, N, look, there was none of u dat convinced Job, or dat answered his words:
Lest y’all should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.
Now he has not directed his words against me: neither will I answer him wit ur speeches.
Dey were amazed, dey answered no more: dey left off speakin.
When I had waited, (4 dey spoke not, but stood still, N answered no more;)

4 I am full of matter, tha spirit within me constraineth me.

Let me not, I pray u, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles 2 man.
4 I know not 2 give flattering titles; in so doin my maker would soon take me away.

33.text: So, Job, I pray u, hear my speeches, N listen 2 all my words.

Look, in dis u r not just: I will answer u, dat God is greater than man.

4 God speaks once, yeah twice, yet man perceiveth it not.

Then he opens tha ears of men, N sealeth their instruction,
Dat he may withdraw man from his purpose, N hide pride from man.

So dat his life abhorreth bread, N his soul dainty food.

Yeah, his soul draws near 2 tha grave, N his life 2 tha destroyers.

Look, all dese things works God oftentimes wit man,
2 bring back his soul from tha pit, 2 be enlightened wit tha light of tha livin.

34.text: Furthermore Elihu answered,

4 tha ear trieth words, as tha mouth tasteth food.

4 Job has said, I am righteous: N God has taken away my judgment.

36.text: Elihu also proceeded, N said,

37.text: At dis also my heart trembleth, N is moved out of his place.

38.text: Then tha LORD answered Job out of tha whirlwind, N said,

39.text: Know u tha time when tha wild goats of tha rock bring forth? or can u mark when tha hinds do calve?

40.text: Moreover tha LORD answered Job, N said,

Then Job answered tha LORD, N said,

Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yeah, twice; but I will proceed no further.
Then answered tha LORD 2 Job out of tha whirlwind, N said,
Gird up ur loins now like a man: I will demand of u, N declare u 2 me.
Will u also disannul my judgment? will u condemn me, dat u may be righteous?
Have u an arm like God? or can u thunder wit a voice like him?
Deck urself now wit majesty N excellency; N array urself wit glory N beauty.
Cast abroad tha rage of ur wrath: N look every one dat is proud, N abase him.
Look on every one dat is proud, N bring him low; N tread down tha wicked in their place.
Hide ’em in tha dust together; N bind their faces in secret.
Then will I also confess 2 u dat ur own right hand can save u.
Look now behemoth, which I made wit u; he eats grass as an ox.
Look now, his strength is in his loins, N his force is in tha navel of his belly.
He moveth his tail like a cedar: tha sinews of his stones r wrapped together.
His bones r as strong pieces of brass; his bones r like bars of iron.
He is tha chief of tha ways of God: he dat made him can make his sword 2 approach 2 him.
Surely tha mountains bring him forth food, where all tha beasts of tha field play.
He lies under tha shady trees, in tha covert of tha reed, N fens.
Tha shady trees cover him wit their shadow; tha willows of tha brook compass him about.
Look, he drinks up a river, N hurries not: he trusts dat he can draw up Jordan in2 his mouth.
He takes it wit his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.

41.text: Can u draw out leviathan wit an hook? or his tongue wit a cord which u lettest down?
Can u put an hook in2 his nose? or bore his jaw through wit a thorn?
Will he make many supplications 2 u? will he speak soft words 2 u?
Will he make a covenant wit u? will u take him 4 a servant 4 ever?
Will u play wit him as wit a bird? or will u bind him 4 ur maidens?
Shall tha companions make a banquet of him? shall dey part him among tha merchants?
Can u fill his skin wit barbed irons? or his head wit fish spears?
Lay thine hand upon him, remember tha battle, do no more.
Look, tha hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at tha sight of him?
None is so fierce dat dare stir him up: who then is able 2 stand before me?
Who has prevented me, dat I should repay him? whatever is under tha whole heaven is mine.
I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
Who can discover tha face of his garment? or who can come 2 him wit his double bridle?
Who can open tha doors of his face? his teeth r terrible round about.
His scales r his pride, shut up together as wit a close seal.
One is so near 2 another, dat no air can come between ’em.
Dey r joined one 2 another, dey stick together, dat dey cannot be sundered.
By his neesings a light does shine, N his eyes r like tha eyelids of tha morning.
Out of his mouth go burnin lamps, N sparks of fire leap out.
Out of his nostrils goes smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
His breath kindleth coals, N a flame goes out of his mouth.
In his neck remains strength, N sorrow is turned in2 joy before him.
Tha flakes of his flesh r joined together: dey r firm in themselves; dey cannot be moved.
His heart is as firm as a stone; yeah, as hard as a piece of tha nether millstone.
When he raises up himself, tha mighty r afraid: by reason of breakings dey purify themselves.
Tha sword of him dat lays at him cannot hold: tha spear, tha dart, nor tha habergeon.
He esteemeth iron as straw, N brass as rotten wood.
Tha arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones r turned wit him in2 stubble.
Darts r counted as stubble: he laugheth at tha shaking of a spear.
Sharp stones r under him: he spreads sharp pointed things upon tha mire.
He makes tha deep 2 boil like a pot: he makes tha sea like a pot of ointment.
He makes a path 2 shine after him; one would think tha deep 2 be hoary.
Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.
He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all tha children of pride.

42.text: Then Job answered tha LORD, N said,
I know dat u can do every thing, N dat no thought can be withholden from u.
Who is he dat hides counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered dat I understood not; things too wonderful 4 me, which I knew not.
Hear, I beg u, N I will speak: I will demand of u, N declare u 2 me.
I have heard of u by tha hearin of tha ear: but now mine eye sees u.
So I abhor myself, N repent in dust N ashes.

N it was so, dat after tha LORD had spoken dese words 2 Job, tha LORD said 2 Eliphaz tha Temanite, My wrath is kindled against u, N against ur two friends: 4 y’all have not spoken of me tha thing dat is right, as my servant Job has.

Therefore take 2 u now seven bullocks N seven rams, N go 2 my servant Job, N offer up 4 y’all a burnt offering; N my servant Job shall pray 4 u: 4 him will I accept: lest I deal wit u after ur folly, in dat y’all have not spoken of me tha thing which is right, like my servant Job.
So Eliphaz tha Temanite N Bildad tha Shuhite N Zophar tha Naamathite went, N did according as tha LORD commanded ’em: tha LORD also accepted Job.
N tha LORD turned tha captivity of Job, when he prayed 4 his friends: also tha LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then came there 2 him all his brothers, N all his sisters, N all dey dat had been of his acquaintance before, N did eat bread wit him in his house: N dey bemoaned him, N comforted him over all tha evil dat tha LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, N every one an earring of gold.
So tha LORD blessed tha latter end of Job more than his beginning: 4 he had fourteen thousand sheep, N six thousand camels, N a thousand yoke of oxen, N a thousand she asses.

N he called tha name of tha first, Jemima; N tha name of tha second, Kezia; N tha name of tha third, Keren-happuch.
N in all tha land were no women found so fair as tha daughters of Job: N their father gave ’em inheritance among their brothers.
